page: Microsoft Azure L128as_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine within the Lasv5 series, built on x86_64 AMD processors and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 128 dedicated vCPUs paired with 1024.0 GB of RAM, yielding an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of memory per core. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The primary architectural distinction of the L128as_v5 is its direct-attached NVMe SSD storage subsystem, which delivers 30,718 GB of bundled local space. The configuration also supports Azure Premium Storage for external disk volumes. This high-density local NVMe array allows workloads to bypass external network storage latency, maximizing throughput for read- and write-intensive data streams.

Resource efficiency is achieved by consolidating 128 dedicated processing threads, one terabyte of volatile memory, and substantial high-speed local disk capacity within a single host instance. Primary tradeoffs involve managing the ephemeral nature of direct-attached NVMe storage and planning network access without default public IPv4 addressing. The machine profile fits large transactional databases, distributed NoSQL engines, search indexing clusters, and enterprise analytics pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure L128as_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance based on AMD x86_64 architecture running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system features 128 dedicated vCPUs and 1024.0 GB of system memory, delivering a balanced 8.0 GB of RAM per core without discrete GPU hardware. A principal differentiator is its massive integrated local NVMe SSD storage tier, offering 30,718 GB of direct-attached space alongside Premium Storage capabilities. This high-capacity local storage structure significantly reduces I/O latency for IOPS-intensive applications. Economically and architecturally, the instance consolidates substantial compute, extensive volatile memory, and low-latency disk capacity within a single envelope. It is appropriate for large-scale data engineering tasks, enterprise relational database management systems, distributed NoSQL databases, search indexing engines, and high-throughput analytics pipelines requiring rapid scratch space and high data retention on local disks.
